- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 92+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to reflect this, often holding high values.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values are trending lower.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late, missing the true turning point.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility spikes; tends to smooth out sharp drops or rises, leading to lagged corrections.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often underreacts — fails to anticipate the next dip, especially if preceded by a spike.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the last 5–10 days of history show a clear downward trend — model underperforms when history is flat or rising.
